svg.text: PLATE — the link that was dimensioned but never drawn
WHAT HOLDS THE MONITOR
Part C, the plate. The display bolts to it, it bolts to the struts, and the struts stand on the floor. The fridge carries none of the weight.
PLATE 297 x 152.2 vs THE REAR BOX, IN PORTRAIT
REAR BOX 134 x 260 — DIMENSIONED
GPIO slot ~R107
clears the plate by 31
FAN ~R82, ~30 dia
plate laps it by 9.1
both SCALED off the raster,
not dimensioned by Waveshare
VESA 100 — DIMENSIONED
to strut
box 134 wide
strut bolts 246 — clear the box by 56 each side
plate 296.6
the plate is 152.2 TALL inside a 260 box — it sits wholly on the box face
and laps the fan by 9.1 mm, which is what the 14.1 mm notch removes
THE CHAIN
THE DISPLAY
4 x M4 into the VESA inserts, on SPACERS
THE PLATE
4 bolts at 246 x 101.6 into the strut
slots
THE STRUTS
x2
stand on
THE FEET
x2
rest on
THE FLOOR
THE CLAMP BARS x2
Grip the fridge top and its underside.
They carry ZERO weight — they only
stop the frame falling away from the
panel.
SO, WHAT HOLDS IT?
Nothing holds it TO the fridge. The FLOOR
holds it up, the way a bookcase stands on
the floor and leans on a wall. The fridge
only stops it tipping away.
That is the whole point of the change. The
magnet design really did hang off the
fridge, so every question was about how
hard it gripped. Here the grip carries
nothing, so a non-magnetic panel, paint
creep and peel all stop mattering.
A solid plate over the Pi's fan and GPIO
cooks it. The old plate was 279 tall
purely to carry vent WINDOWS over that
region. At 152.2 the plate clears the GPIO
slot entirely (31 mm clear) and needs only
to deal with the fan, which an edge notch
does far more cheaply than an enclosed
window.
The 2 edge notches are NOT idle insurance
— correcting an earlier claim here.
Reading the fan off Waveshare's drawing
puts it at ~R82, so the plate edge laps it
by 9.1 mm and the notch is what uncovers
it. Depth 14.1 is derived: fan near edge
minus 5 mm for the fact that every one of
those figures is SCALED off a raster, not
dimensioned.
Bolt rows are 101.6 apart — exactly 2 slot
pitches, so both sit identically in their
slots. Putting them ABOVE and BELOW the
box instead needs 6 pitches and a plate
2.3x taller, whose edge would reach past
the Pi opening and bring the vent windows
back.
ORIENTATION IS FORCED. Landscape would
hang 41.5 mm off the REAR edge and cannot
be slid forward: the clamp must stay
inside the 406.6 mm window.
Heads sit on the DISPLAY side, so they
must not fall under the Pi bump-out. In
portrait the box is 134 wide and the bolts
246 apart, clearing by 56 mm — because the
STRUT SPACING is wider than the box, not
by luck of where the holes went.
CONSEQUENCE: those heads are unreachable
once the display is on. The plate goes on
the struts BEFORE the display.
